requirements.statement: Apply the general p.6 deployment procedure when no scenario specifies deployment: both sides roll initiative, winner chooses entry edge and loser takes the opposite, and each selected Mech walks, runs or jumps onto its assigned edge counting MP from the first full hex.
requirements.reviewNote: Printed p.6 general setup: current Legacy.reset initializes all units inside the board at fixed coordinates; initiative goes directly to move and makeRuntime preserves that placement. The non-scenario initiative edge choice, opposite entry edges and border entry MP accounting are absent. Scenario-specific placement remains separate. Initial engine implementation: separate setup initiative and replay-safe choice, six opposite axial edges, offboard exclusion from occupancy, walk/run first full hex terrain cost and continuation, jump first-hex accounting. Existing scenario unchanged. Layout convention: facing along inward axis and external origin at first full hex surface. UI/server configuration, blocked or immobile entry and complete browser/server tests remain; status stays known_missing. Local browser now exposes standard setup from New Battle, edge selection for hotseat/player winners, entry mode and legal hex selection, hides undeployed models/arcs, animates entry from virtual origin, preserves scenario restart option. Browser regression covers edge selection then first entry. Fixed offboard jump MP using no inherited dummy water depth. Server contract selection and no-legal-entry behavior still pending. Server operations now store explicit scenario/standard deployment on the draft, default old records to scenario, initialize standard mode only on launch, and resume from persisted Game state. Integration test covers invalid selection, edge choice, mandatory entry, MP and phase transition; browser mission briefing verifies explicit standard selection. Blocked/immobile edge handling and full CI verification remain open. Follow-up: p.11 minimum running entry consumes the movement selection and running heat; p.9 limits ground descent to two levels given the documented external-surface convention. AI prefers another legally selectable mech before reporting blocked deployment. Truly blocked entry is reported without inventing destruction, forfeiture, reward or deferred entry; scenario adjudication remains outside the explicit p.6 rule. Keep known_missing until remaining setup edge cases and CI are verified. Undeployed units are additionally excluded from weapon and physical previews, AI target scoring, skids and displacement occupancy, preventing phantom contacts at their legacy coordinates. Passing through a friendly occupied entry hex and complete no-entry scenario behavior still require review. Printed pp.6,9,11 friendly occupancy: ground entry can transit a dry nonhazardous friendly-occupied first hex using the normal remaining-MP pathfinder; the full first-hex cost and both travel hexes are recorded, endpoints remain unoccupied, enemy occupancy is not bypassed. Hazardous occupied first hexes (immediate PSR or skid) and full blocked scenario adjudication remain explicitly open. Two regression tests; exact CI pending. Subsequent original-book pp.11–12 comparison: normal on-map jumping now uses a monotonic shortest-path search, matching standard deployment rather than a single interpolated line; both occupied intermediate hexes and wooded terrain remain passable. Voluntary prone posture consumes one MP and rejects jumping, no MP, or wrong phase. UI and API preserve declared ground mode. Added three engine and one validation regressions, exact CI pending. Broader movement rules remain separately auditable. Original pp.9,11,40,42: friendly-occupied water/rubble entry resolves terrain PSR before any onward movement, retains its dice, and resolves involuntary stacking with the existing domino routine. Ordinary transit permits prone friendly occupants but never them as destinations. Building/skid first-hex transit and completely blocked initial deployment remain explicitly outside this patch; movement-time optional domino dodge still uses existing fallback, not an interactive choice. Two deterministic regressions; exact CI pending. Human ground-move orders (including entry) now use the replay journal for an interactive domino choice before committing the move; the choice resumes the original server-authorized command even with a nonempty movement queue. The replay journal is private, and resumed animation identifies the original moving Mech. AI-initiated movement and charge-generated displacement still use fallback; exact CI pending. Follow-up: movement replay now covers AI-generated moves and charge/DFA approach orders. The server pauses its AI loop for a human domino victim and resumes the original authorized action without accepting direct client AI commands. An involuntarily interrupted approach consumes the selection but cannot fabricate a physical declaration. Added two engine and one API regression, exact CI pending. AGoAC pp.6,9,11–12: minimum movement uses one available walking MP even when a lost leg forbids ordinary running, including offboard entry; it is limited to the Movement Phase, cannot change a committed mode or bypass ammo dumping, resolves entry terrain checks, and consumes the selection. Four regressions. Exact CI pending. Printed pp.6,11–12: jumping entry and ordinary jumping now accept a free six-way landing orientation before terrain PSRs; a failed water landing uses this orientation for fall facing, and subsequent ordinary rotate is forbidden after jumping. UI/API expose and validate jump-only facing; four regressions. CI pending. AI continues to choose its default facing; charge/DFA approach is a separate declaration path. Printed p.12: one-legged biped standing now records its single cumulative PSR and suppresses the duplicate running-damage PSR at selection completion, retaining standing and running heat and ordinary running PSRs. Flag resets at End Phase. Two regressions; exact CI pending. Quad extensions remain outside this AGoAC change. Printed pp.9,11–12: rotation commits the selected ground movement mode, including while prone; standing may not change a committed mode and the UI/API now convey the chosen mode and free successful-standing facing, including minimum stand. Five engine/API regressions; exact CI pending. Advanced rules unchanged except shared command validation. 2026-11-18 printed p.6 checked against p.9 and p.11: fixed first-hex friendly transit on pavement and buildings without adding new building/skid rules; call existing building resolution before normal on-map transit; reject repeated setup and jumping when prone at start. All 12 combinations of winning team and hexagonal-map edge now have a complete ground entry regression. The original does not adjudicate a scenario where no legal entry exists; continue to surface that blocker instead of inventing damage or forfeiture. Remaining p.6 inventory: map/force selection prior to play and mutual agreement for custom mechs, plus exact CI for new tests. Fixed single hexagonal board is a digital layout convention, not the printed mapsheet layout. Setup force selection is now separately tracked in agoac-047. Entry-transit patch #117 passed all three workflow checks and was merged. General mapa selection and complete acceptance still pending; do not treat 047 tests as certification of every setup combination. Digital map selection and six-way rotation tracked separately in 048. Original mapsheet composition and scenario-fixed layouts remain outstanding. Local scoped slot selection is verified; larger rosters, full original map arrangements, scenario setup and authoritative campaign choices remain unverified. Joined rectangular native map layout added under 049; Setup remains open for complete original scenarios, arbitrary maps, larger forces and full acceptance. Scoped one/two-sheet composition verified after #120; expanded local forces tracked under agoac-050. Setup inventory remains open for broader map/roster and scenario options. Final exact #121 CI review: all 40 linked cases passed; server standard deployment smoke passed. Scope restricted to p.6 generic deployment. Specific printed scenarios remain open under agoac-scenarios, and general movement/advanced timing remain in their chapters.

Independent two-die draws for each team, equal sums loop, higher sum wins; buildQueue starts with loser when both forces have surviving units. requirements.statement: Remaining Sequence of Play exceptions and victory conditions: initiative-consistent resolution including no-fire selections and displacement exceptions; permanent mutual inability to move and damage; alternatives agreed before play.
requirements.reviewNote: Printed pp.6-7 and 30: buildQueue includes surviving immobile and unarmed units and declarations are stored. However resolveFire interleaves to-hit rolls with damage rather than an all-attacks-first stage; resolvePhysical processes charge declarations in unit-array order before other declarations; heat avoidance lacks an explicit conscious-pilot restriction; inherited checkWin handles last-side elimination but has no stalemate draw predicate. Split these into atomic follow-up implementation and regression requirements; do not infer complete timing from green CI. Follow-up separates ordinary weapon to-hit and ammo expenditure from damage and groups damage by target. Physical staging, selectable independent damage ordering, heat and stalemate remain outstanding. Thermal avoidance now distinguishes unconscious/unavailable pilots and automatic below-14 restart; voluntary shutdown/restart and phase PSR interactions remain independently auditable. Ordinary physical attack rolls now staged before ordinary damage, using initiative and immediate displacement exception. Same-side interactive resolution and full charge/DFA effects remain incomplete. Controller can now choose physical attacker order when their side has a remaining displacement-capable attack, grouped by attacker; ordinary weapon damage order is separate. Weapon resolution now offers independent controller choices of target group and weapon for to-hit rolls and successful damage, using the existing replay journal. All declared attacks still roll before any damage. Target groups stay contiguous and each cluster resolves fully. AI uses deterministic declaration order. Controller choice of Mech resolution order and complete victory/heat audit remain open. Browser regression exercises the independent order prompts, authoritative payload and reconnect. At the Mech level, the player can independently select a remaining attacker in each existing initiative-based team slot for the to-hit and damage stage, before selecting that Mech's target/weapon order. Existing declaration ordering supplies the team slots; AI uses declaration order. Added replay regression, with victory/End Phase edge cases and exact CI still pending. Heat ammunition explosion follows p.38 maximum damage per shot; equal-value nonempty bins are now a controller decision, journaled after the failed avoidance roll with no reroll on resume. AI retains deterministic most-rounds fallback. Added deterministic tests; other victory/End Phase cases and exact CI remain pending. Printed p.7: elimination is now checked at the movement boundary too. Permanent mutual lack of movement and damage is checked after End Phase using recovered/cooled capability bounds; surviving in-range weapons and possible adjacent physical attacks prevent a draw. Conservative detection deliberately does not certify map-trapped cases or permanently blocked LOS/attack arcs. The campaign's documented 12-round limit is a separate scenario policy, not the standard AGoAC victory rule. Five new engine regressions; exact CI and remaining cases not yet verified. Original pp.7,38,44: voluntary shutdown/restart is available directly in End Phase, with existing Movement preselection retained as a shortcut. Controller must be available when executing a queued command. Server End Phase authorization is restricted to the owning side. Initiative snapshots actual unconsciousness before the turn, avoiding stale recovery eligibility. Four engine/API regressions. Selection by a pilot who first recovers during End Phase remains a separate UI timing case; exact CI pending. Printed pp.7,38,44: a newly recovered pilot receives the otherwise unavailable End Phase voluntary reactor choice after the successful consciousness roll. Interactive End Phase replay retains the roll, restart is excluded at 30+ heat, and unsuccessful recovery does not prompt. AI fallback retains state. Three engine/API regressions; CI pending. Printed pp.6–7: after a selection, remove queue slots exceeding the count of surviving unselected Mechs, preserving immobile survivors and relative order. Recomputing later pair ratios after mid-phase casualties remains open. Three new regressions; exact CI pending. Pair-aware rebatching implemented in this PR; legacy save limitation documented under agoac-005. Exact CI pending. Re-reviewed printed pp.6–7, including attack declaration immutability and all five listed End Phase actions. Added a no-reroll immutable declaration and torso/arm lock test. Remaining detailed phase resolution and victory/stalemate audit stays open. Do not treat passing ratio tests as complete resolution-order evidence. Printed pp.6,40: movement-phase damage must not accumulate into weapon-phase PSRs. Found missing movement boundary cleanup; ensure remaining pending PSRs and consciousness rolls are resolved before building fire declarations, with their roll record retained. Two exact regressions prepared; this boundary safety net does not certify precise immediate triggering of PSRs during every damaging movement action, which remains part of movement/PSR audit. Printed pp.7,19,25: correct conservative stalemate detection for permanently prone bipeds. They cannot perform physical attacks; cannot fire with a destroyed arm or fire leg weapons. A temporarily prone unit with recoverable movement does not trigger a draw. Three regressions prepared. Other conservative false negatives (e.g. permanent LOS obstacles and permanently unusable facing) remain explicitly open. Exact #125 CI + browser: all 36 previously linked cases passed, tested and merged trees match (9d3b1d14028c90de4194d0a3f81bcb5666de6ab2). Printed pp.7,19,28–29: refine conservative stalemate capability for zero-ground-MP standing bipeds with unusable hip/arm combinations; preserve a possible push with two arms and shoulder modifiers. Permanently separate dry and fully submerged firing domains, use underwater range for a permanently submerged shooter. Three new regressions pending. Depth-one transitions, permanently blocked LOS/facing, map trapping, and alternative victory conditions by mutual agreement still not fully certified. No chapter completion claimed. Exact #126: all 39 linked cases passed; four independently scoped completed requirements extracted as 051–054 without certifying the whole chapter. Printed pp.7,13,19–21: immutable high dry hill on a straight full-hex row can block direct fire permanently; retain possible indirect fire. A permanently prone biped has fixed facing. Two new tests pending. Conservative map trapping, split LOS, indirect spotter eligibility and arbitrary agreed victory conditions remain open; do not infer full overall victory parity. Printed pp.7,13: immutable straight dry hill adjacent to either endpoint blocks at that endpoint's maximum standing height, regardless of the other endpoint height. Apply the same conservative obstruction to actual LOS to avoid disagreement with stalemate. New regression checks symmetry, boundary below threshold and nonadjacent low hill. General split LOS and full elevation rules remain for combat audit. Exact CI pending. Printed pp.7,13,21: indirect fire is limited to LRM launchers; another friendly unit needs LOS. Conservative stalemate detection now rejects permanently hill-blocked LRMs without a possible separate spotter and no longer treats SRMs as indirect-capable. Fixed-facing prone weapon arcs are also checked for launchers. Spotter LOS uses only proven immutable hill obstruction; split LOS, water and other constraints remain open. New regression and updated prior hill test; exact CI pending. Printed pp.7,25 directly rechecked: immobile adjacent units separated by more than one terrain level cannot make ordinary physical attacks. Conservative capability now excludes those pairs only if neither can move, preserving possible DFA. Tests cover differences -2..2. Exact CI pending. Other physical attack eligibility and alternative agreed victory conditions remain open. Printed pp.7,25,28–29 directly reviewed: permanent fixed biped physical capability respects actual feet facing (not torso twist), arm-side arcs, flooded limbs, and dry versus entirely submerged targets. Retains conservative potential front push/club and kick; other posture and elevation combinations remain open. Quad path remains outside base-rule certification. Exact CI pending. Original CAT3500D printed p.15 directly inspected: arm reversal is prohibited for a weapon split across an arm and torso; reversed arms and nonzero torso twist cannot coexist in a declaration. Added production guards and regression, source/dist synchronized. Detailed fire-arc and construction audits remain separate. Prepared on PR #131 exact head; not yet tested or published as a PR. Printed p.19 waterline constraints: a fixed prone depth-one target is fully submerged, and leg-mounted weapons on a standing depth-one Mech fire below the surface. Apply these constraints to stalemate capability while preserving potential recovery and torso-mounted fire above the surface. New regression; exact CI pending. Full LOS and underwater fire audit remains open. Scope limited to printed pp.6–7 Sequence of Play / Victory Conditions: after a completed phase determines a winner or draw, do not transition into or announce another phase; clear acting controller state. Added 12 phase/outcome regression combinations and checks against additional phase execution. Physical hit-table and attack formula changes deferred to their own chapter. Exact CI pending; alternative pre-game agreed conditions and conservative stalemate remain open. Direct source review of original printed p.7 (Victory Conditions): other conditions may be agreed before play. Implemented an explicitly optional digital round-limit draw preset (not a mandatory printed turn limit), two-side pregame consent in local setup, locked terms and complete-round evaluation with normal elimination taking precedence. AI accepts the optional preset by design; server campaign rules unchanged. Arbitrary custom victory objectives remain open. Engine regression added; browser validation pending. Browser regression also covers both-side approval, invalidation on changes to agreed terms, and starting the configured game. Original CAT3500D printed pp.6–7, inspected rendered pages in this session: resolution of weapons begins again with the initiative loser, one Mech at a time, after declarations; the unequal-force ratio rule explicitly describes declarations. Previously a loser passing its first selection could leave the winning side first in the filtered declaration sequence. Rebuild roll/damage order from nonempty attack records, loser first with one-per-side alternation until exhausted; keep controller choice within each side, leave no-fire declaration consumption intact. Alternating resolution slots are the digital implementation of the one-Mech-at-a-time rule. Added tests for either winner and both empty/hold forms. Prepared; exact CI pending. No changes to hit tables, attack formulas or geometry. Visually inspected CAT3500D printed p.7 Physical Attack Phase and p.6 Resolving Weapons Fire (same steps apply, except torso/arms). Ordinary physical resolution now groups a Mech's declared attacks and alternates eligible Mechs starting with initiative loser, independent of declaration order and no-attack selections. Existing displacement exception ordering is intentionally unchanged. Alternation is the implementation interpretation of one-Mech-at-a-time resolution, not a new attack rule. Added both-winner regression covering all ordinary rolls before damage, grouped punches, unequal eligible counts, and preservation of displacement ordering. Exact CI pending. No hit or damage mechanics changed. CAT3500D printed p.7 visually inspected in this turn. Support free-text pre-agreed custom victory objectives in local two-human hotseat, with two-party confirmation of the result at a completed-round boundary or after standard terminal outcome. Text is not executable and is displayed via textContent. Standard elimination remains fallback and may be overridden once by the agreed manual verdict. This is a digital adjudication design, not a mandatory printed procedure; AI/server campaign and automated arbitrary objectives unchanged. Unit/UI tests pending. Re-read printed pp.6–7 visually in the current session. Browser failure on option isDisabled assertion addressed by checking the native disabled property; expanded actual full-round verdict interaction and stale-approval regression. Replaced ambiguous negation assignment in verdict UI to avoid known S2757. Exact revised checks pending. Printed p.7 visually checked: a draw requires mutual inability to move and damage. Recovered only the human-adjudication portion of deferred/agoac-stalemate-review (df87f7fd5e875d1a1fd60e056be73f0f39f2d2a8); geometry/canEverDamage, hit tables, and all later-chapter mechanics stay deferred. The optional hotseat confirmation records players' adjudication after a complete turn (not automatic proof and not mandated by the book). Both sides must affirm both conditions; no AI or server use. Engine and browser regressions prepared; exact CI pending. Known dependency on completeness of automatic capability checks remains disclosed. Original printed p.6 explicitly requires every declared attack to be made even if its intended target is destroyed by an earlier attack. Added an isolated two-attacker regression for both ordinary phases: both attack rolls and weapon heat expenditures occur, the destroyed target's second declared attack remains recorded, and the model is removed at the phase boundary. Uses existing engine behavior; no attack resolution mathematics, hit tables or geometry altered. Exact CI pending. requirements.statement: A Mech whose pilot dies is removed from the map at the end of that phase; preserve same-phase attack declarations and resolve occupancy and displacement until removal.
requirements.reviewNote: Printed pp.35 and 44 require phase-end map removal. Actual wound/destroyLocation marks dead immediately; movement occupancy and displacement ignore dead units before phase transition; the UI collapses a dead model but has no explicit phase-boundary removal state. Already-declared ordinary weapon attacks can still roll. Keep destruction and on-map presence distinct and audit displacement, immediate fall damage, persistence, and presentation together. Partial implementation in follow-up: standard lethal damage records pending phase-end map removal; historical state and ordinary attack declarations are retained. Full domino, fall, charge/DFA and simultaneous damage ordering remain to be independently audited. Keep known_missing until those interactions are covered. Ordinary weapon attack staging now spends ammunition and rolls all attacks before damage; pending verification in CI. Follow-up corrects ordinary charge into prohibited displacement terrain (pp.26,42): both units retain positions and damage/PSRs remain; lethal target is not displaced. Existing fractional charge-damage rounding is confirmed by the 65-ton/5-hex example. DFA alternatives, dominoes and physical interruption remain unresolved. Follow-up: opposed pushes resolve both attempts before any displacement, both successful attempts leave both positions unchanged and require immediate PSRs; prohibited push retains positions and requires PSR. Domino and accidental falls remain outstanding. Domino chain now checks standing targets before displacement, falls in destination on failure, ignores fall-avoidance checks for prone targets and destroys a blocked terminal target. Optional controller-chosen dodge and occupied downward displacement (accidental falls from above) remain missing; no claim of complete rule. Accidental fall branch now distinguishes occupied downward displacement, target movement/terrain to-hit, punch packet damage with full-submersion halving, rear fall, destination selection and victim PSR. Remaining: interactive dodge, already occupied alternative landing candidates, exact two-stage water falling damage and full physical precedence audit. p.43 follow-up: forced dry-to-water descent passes origin elevation into fall; surface and bottom independently rounded and packetized. Same-water fall remains halved once. Voluntary water-entry and jump-landing semantics pending separate Movement audit. Follow-up (pp.25–29): reserve each displacement target across charge/DFA/push, reject charge/DFA against unfinished special attackers and ordinary physical attacks against DFA, preserve reciprocal pushes, permit DFA against prone completed targets. General displacement priority and optional dodge remain unresolved. Physical phase follows losing-side priority for conflicting orders, then checks current geometry against pre-attack damage state. Ordinary attack rolls are staged before ordinary damage; displacement can invalidate an unmade attack. Same-side order is a stable default, not yet interactive. Special damage/displacement interleaving and geometric effects are bounded to current implementation. DFA landing follow-up (pp.27–28): legal angular alternative groups for successful DFA, all legal adjacent options on missed DFA (including occupied and offboard), forbidden all-neighbor destruction, airborne stacking exemption, rear fall on miss and original start hex attack direction. Resolver still defaults to first legal direction; interactive controller choice remains missing. Interactive displacement: successful side-entry domino PSR now offers optional forward/backward dodge under unused MP, legal geometry, standing/mobile and movement-mode restrictions; DFA target controller chooses legal displacement destination. Local and authoritative phase resolution pauses on a controller choice, replays previous RNG samples instead of rerolling, redacts private journal from public snapshots and validates decisions. Automated battles retain deterministic default. Full browser interaction and immediate Weapon Phase DFA miss/PSR semantics require separate verification. Browser regression now covers pause, reload, exact server version/choice payload, no phase transition until selection, and the resulting selected hex (server route fixture backed by the shared rules engine). Same-controller physical ordering: before a side's pending displacement-capable attacks, offer successive attacker selection; keep initiative priority and pair reciprocal pushes. Conservatively offer the choice even when a possible domino chain ultimately does not interrupt another attack. UI uses saved choice mechanism. This does not yet certify every immediate-damage interaction. Weapon Attack Phase airborne DFA fall exception: a failed PSR or automatic fall immediately resolves the missed DFA landing and rear two-level impact, using the triggering PSR TN for the seat-belt check. Retain resolved declaration reservation, clear airborne and suppress repeated Physical Phase DFA; target chooses legal adjacent displacement using the existing phase-choice mechanism. Direct regressions cover pass/fail, unconsciousness, leg/gyro automatic fall and interactive selection. Source p27–28,40,44; LOS height, destroyed airborne unit and full special-attack timing remain separately auditable. Consolidated scope review of original CAT3500D pp.30,35,42,44. The recorded requirement is about pilot death, phase-end removal, same-phase declarations and displacement effects, not a certificate for every rule in the physical-combat chapter. Added actual lethal head-hit tests through both full attack phases (including outgoing damage after death, temporary occupancy, inability to act, preserved historical unit, removal on transition), and real push/PSR/seat-belt death invalidating an unmade kick. Corrected physical revalidation for immediate deaths during displacement/falls. Standard movement occupancy uses pending map presence; displace explicitly does not apply domino/PSR to a destroyed unit (p.42 no displacement for a unit destroyed by the action; p.35 no further effects after removal). The source does not explicitly define an independent forced entry into a pending destroyed unit's hex; no new behavior invented for this ambiguous interaction. Partial progress notes above refer to earlier revisions; dome dodge and player choice now implemented. Keep as tested_case until exact new CI, Smoke, Browser, and independent source/edge-case review. Broader attack-damage timing/order, deployment and other DFA details are not certified by closing this scoped requirement and remain in subsequent audit scope. Final scoped source and log review: all named tests passed in #114; merged tree equals tested tree.
